plain.fix: short: In the four trials reviewed, no medicine clearly eased withdrawal or craving more than a dummy pill. | but: The review found only four small trials, so a small benefit could have been missed. | how 2: One medicine helped people stay in treatment more than a dummy pill did, but it is no longer sold. | how 4: The review gave no side-effect results for any of the trials.
plain.note: 'So far' and 'only four have been done' stretch a 2009 review (searches to 2008) to today. One small trial reported less withdrawal with mirtazapine. It is the review, not the trials, that is silent on side effects. How 2 lacked its comparison.

plain.fix: short: After one of the larger doses, people slept less and worse that night than after a dummy dose. | how 3: With the biggest dose, the monitor showed about two hours less sleep than with the dummy dose, and more waking than with any other dose.
plain.note: The lowest dose changed no sleep measure, and measured sleep fell only after the biggest dose, so 'after one dose' says more than the paper. How 3 lacked its comparison.

plain.fix: how 3: After the biggest dose, their heart beat faster and blood pressure was higher than after the dummy dose.
plain.note: Heart rate and blood pressure were raised only after the biggest dose (Table 1); the other lines match.
Matches the trial and registry: open label, both groups improved a lot, baseline anxiety 16.5 vs 11.9. 'Hope may explain part' is a hedged inference of the editors, not the paper's.

plain.fix: short: Studies report less craving with exercise than without, but the review that lists them does not say how much less. | how 1: One review listed studies, mostly from compulsory drug rehabilitation centres in China. | how 2: The review says craving went down during and after exercise, compared with control groups. | how 3: The review says it checked study quality but reports no results.
plain.note: It is the review, not all research, that gives no numbers. The review says 'compulsory drug rehabilitation institutions'. We see only the review, not the original authors. The review claims an AMSTAR2 check but reports nothing.

plain.fix: but: One small study of 20 people in a hospital unit; daytime light and withdrawal from other drugs were not controlled.
plain.note: The authors argue that the fixed bedtime did not drive the worsening (the placebo results matched their flexible-bedtime study). The limits they do list include daytime light and withdrawal from other substances.

plain.fix: how 2: Machines in a sleep lab measured their sleep on several nights over three weeks. | how 3: People on modafinil had more deep sleep than those on the dummy pill and, in the third week, more sleep overall. | how 4: They did not feel they slept better, and the study did not check whether it helped them stay off cocaine.
plain.note: Sleep was recorded on nights 1-3, 7-9 and 14-16, not every night. How 3 lacked its comparison. 'Nobody checked' reaches beyond this study.
